rows.rationale: From the plotted values: left limit at 0 is -2, f(1)=2, right limit at -2 is -2; sum -2.
After dividing by x+1>0, both bounding expressions tend to 5 as x→-1+.
Since f(x)/x has a finite limit, f(x)/x²→0; the requested ratio tends to 12/3=4.
Continuity forces numerator zero at 2 and quotient limit 10: a=6,b=-16, hence -10.
As x→-∞, sqrt(4x²+5x-4) is asymptotic to -2x, so the displayed ratio tends to -3/2, not 1/2.
For every real x in the real domain, sqrt(5x-x²)≥0, so sqrt(5x-x²)+5 cannot equal 0; no listed interval contains a root.
Convexity and the second intersection b imply the chord slope on [a,b] exceeds the slope-1 chord from the origin, so f(b)-f(a)>b-a.
The function is 4-(x-1)² with f(-2)=-5. For every a≥1, the range on [-2,a] is [-5,4], difference 9; thus admissible a is unbounded.
Parallel slope-1 tangents occur at x=±1; their intercept difference is 4, so distance is 4/√2=2√2.
At zero, |x| and |x|-x are not differentiable; x|x| and |x³| are differentiable.
The identity reduces to 2x g(x)²=18x⁵, so g=±3x² and f(-1)g(2)=36.
Differentiating the functional identity yields f′(t)=1-t; 1-3a=-14 gives a=5.
Remainder and derivative at 1 give 1+a+b=5 and 7+5a=2; hence 2a+b=3.
Intersection count g jumps at m=-2 and m=-1; continuity of gh forces roots of monic h at both, so h=(x+2)(x+1), h(3)=20.
The limit forces f(0)=0 and f′(0)=3; the inequality requires the remaining quadratic to be nonnegative, giving A≤2 and maximum f(2)=22.
Continuity/differentiability at 1 gives integer solutions (a,b)=(-1,4), so 2a+3b=10.
Using roots (t±√(t²+8))/2, area difference is ((t²+1)/2)√(t²+8), tending to √2.
By the derivative definition, ((x+h)²+2(x+h)+3-(x²+2x+3))/h→2x+2.
For a=7 or larger, the denominator has real zeros not shared with f; for integer a≤6 through 6 inclusive its discriminant is negative, so the quotient is continuous. Maximum is 6.
The two-sided limit fixes f(1)=1 and f′(1)=2, then coefficient comparison gives a=-1,b=-2; differentiating numerator at 1 gives 2f′(2)-f(2)=26.
